title: Electrostatics
source: NCERT Physics Class XII (2026-27 reprint; ch 14 from 2025-26)

children.title: Electric Charge
Why are there exactly two kinds of charge?
children.summary: Rubs glass, amber and fur in every combination; everything sorts into 'like glass' or 'like amber'

children.title: Why does rubbing move electrons, not protons?
children.summary: Zooms into the atoms: only loosely held outer electrons can hop between surfaces

children.title: Why is charge quantised in steps of e?
children.summary: Adds and removes electrons one at a time: q = ne, with e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C

children.title: Why is total charge conserved?
children.summary: Balances the charge ledger before and after rubbing and in pair creation

children.title: Charge a sphere without touching it (induction)
children.summary: Brings a rod near, earths the far side, then removes the earth and the rod

children.title: Gold-leaf electroscope
children.summary: Watches the leaves diverge as charge is shared

children.title: Why does a car door sometimes shock you?
children.summary: Builds up charge by friction while sliding off a seat

children.title: Coulomb's Law
Why does the electric force fall off as 1/r²?
children.summary: Spreads field lines over spheres of area 4πr² (compare gravity)

children.title: Why does gravity lose to electricity by 10³⁹?
children.summary: Compares the electric and gravitational pull between a proton and an electron: about 2.3 × 10³⁹

children.title: Why can forces from many charges simply be added?
children.summary: Places charges one by one and adds their force arrows tip to tail (superposition)

children.title: Net force on a charge
children.summary: Solves 2D configurations by components

children.title: Two charged pith balls
children.summary: Finds the charge from the angle the threads hang at

children.title: Electric Field & Field Lines
Why invent a field at all?
children.summary: Removes the source charge and sees the field 'remembers' it for a while: a field carries energy and information

children.title: Why can't field lines cross, or close on themselves?
children.summary: Tries to draw a crossing (two directions at one point) and a loop (that would make the field non-conservative)

children.title: Why does a dipole's field fall as 1/r³?
children.summary: Moves far from ±q; the two 1/r² fields nearly cancel, leaving a weaker 1/r³ field

children.title: Field-line drawer
children.summary: Places charges and traces the lines

children.title: A dipole in a uniform field
children.summary: Twists a dipole: τ = p × E, and the net force is zero

children.title: Why does a charged comb pick up paper?
children.summary: Induces dipoles in neutral paper so it is pulled into the stronger field

children.title: Flux & Gauss's Law
What is flux? Count the lines through a net
children.summary: Tilts a surface in a field; Φ = E·A, largest face-on

children.title: Why does Gauss's law work for any closed surface?
children.summary: Inflates and dents a surface around a charge; the line count stays q/ε₀ because of the 1/r² law (spec below)
children.spec: Surface: a deformable bubble around a point charge, with field lines drawn. Count: lines leaving the bubble stay constant however it's squashed, giving q/ε₀. Why: area grows as r² while the field falls as 1/r², so each solid-angle wedge carries the same flux. Outside charge: a charge outside sends in as many lines as it takes out, so the net is 0.

children.title: Why is the field inside a charged shell zero?
children.summary: Draws a Gaussian sphere inside: no enclosed charge, so no field

children.title: Why do a wire, a sheet and a sphere give 1/r, constant and 1/r²?
children.summary: Picks the matching Gaussian cylinder, pillbox and sphere for each symmetry

children.title: Choose the Gaussian surface
children.summary: Matches the symmetry to the surface

children.title: Electric Potential
Why does a potential exist at all?
children.summary: Carries a charge around a loop: the work is zero, so the electric force is conservative

children.title: Why is potential 1/r when the field is 1/r²?
children.summary: Integrates the field in from infinity

children.title: Why are equipotentials perpendicular to field lines?
children.summary: Moves along an equipotential: no work, so no field component along it

children.title: Why is E = −dV/dr?
children.summary: Rolls a test charge 'downhill' on a potential landscape

children.title: Potential of charges and dipoles
children.summary: Adds scalar potentials (no arrows needed)

children.title: Potential energy of a system of charges
children.summary: Sums over pairs

children.title: Six charges on a hexagon
children.summary: Finds the potential at the centre

children.title: Conductors & Dielectrics
Why is E = 0 inside a conductor?
children.summary: Watches free electrons rearrange until they feel no force

children.title: Why does charge sit on the surface and crowd at sharp points?
children.summary: Charges a pear-shaped conductor and sees the density highest at the tip (lightning rods)

children.title: Why does a hollow conductor shield its inside, but not its outside?
children.summary: Puts charges outside the cavity and then inside it

children.title: Why does a dielectric weaken the field?
children.summary: Aligns molecular dipoles so that their own field opposes E₀

children.title: Polarisation visualiser
children.summary: Changes the dielectric constant K and watches the effective field

children.title: Why are you safe in a car in a thunderstorm?
children.summary: Lets the metal body act as a shield

children.title: Capacitors
Why does C = Q/V depend only on geometry?
children.summary: Doubles Q and sees V double too, so the ratio is fixed by the shape

children.title: Why is C = ε₀A/d for parallel plates?
children.summary: Widens the plates and narrows the gap

children.title: Why does a dielectric multiply C by K?
children.summary: Slides a slab in: the field falls, so V falls and C rises

children.title: Why do series capacitors add as reciprocals?
children.summary: Sees the same Q on each, so the Vs add; in parallel the same V, so the Qs add

children.title: Where is a capacitor's energy stored?
children.summary: Finds ½CV² as the field energy density ½ε₀E² × volume

children.title: Combination solver
children.summary: Reduces networks step by step

children.title: Camera flash and touchscreens
children.summary: Dumps stored charge in a burst; a fingertip changes C
